{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox Hurling All-Ireland | year = 2001 | image = | dates =15 April - 9 September 2001 | teams = 21 | connacht = | munster = Tipperary | leinster = Kilkenny | ulster = Derry | matches = 19 | poty = [[File: Colours of Tipperary.svg|border|20px]] [[Tommy Dunne]] | team = Tipperary | titles = 25th | captain = [[Tommy Dunne]] | manager = [[Nicky English]] | team2 = Galway | captain2 = [[Liam Hodgins]] | manager2 = [[Noel Lane (Galway hurler)|Noel Lane]] | totalgoals = | totalpoints = | topscorer = [[File: Colours of Galway.svg|border|20px]] [[Eugene Cloonan]] (5–25) | previous = [[2000 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2000]] | next = [[2002 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2002]] }} The '''2001 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 114th staging of [[Ireland]]'s premier hurling knock-out competition. [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] won the championship, beating [[Galway GAA|Galway]] 2–18 to 2–15 in the [[2001 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]] at [[Croke Park]], [[Dublin]]. ==Calendar== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: center" ! Sunday 19 August 2001 |- | All-Ireland Final ||Sunday 9 September 2001 |} ==Format== The All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship was run on a provincial basis as usual. All games were played on a knockout basis whereby once a team lost they were eliminated from the championship. The format for the All-Ireland series of games ran as follows: * The winners of the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] advanced directly to one of the All-Ireland semi-finals. * The winners of the [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|Leinster Championship]] advanced directly to the second All-Ireland semi-final. * The winners of the [[Ulster Senior Hurling Championship|Ulster Championship]] advanced directly to one of the All-Ireland quarter-finals where they were drawn to play [[Galway GAA|Galway]]. The winners of this game would later play the Leinster champions in the All-Ireland semi-final. * The Munster runners-up were drawn to play the Leinster runners-up in the second All-Ireland quarter-final. The winners of this game would later play the Munster champions in the All-Ireland semi-final. == Team changes == === To Championship === Promoted from the [[All-Ireland Intermediate Hurling Championship]] * Kildare * Meath * Wicklow === From Championship === Regraded to the [[All-Ireland Intermediate Hurling Championship]] * Kerry == Teams == === General information === Twenty-one
